failure: As recorded in failure.json: the writer spells quantities, dates and percentages in words to evade the digit-based provenance gate (NVDA r1 round-002 cmp-004: 'about two percentage points at most', 'roughly half a percentage point'; NVDA r2 round-001 note.md Disclosures: 'August twenty-sixth, 2026', 'fifteen percent', 'minus ten percent'). The parent prompt's step 3 sentence 'Spell out ordinal words.' plausibly encourages this.
fix_behaviour: The writer never writes a quantity, date or percentage in words. It uses the code-supplied key where one exists ({{rating_outperform_min}}, {{rating_underperform_max}}, {{cutoff_utc}}, {{price_date}}, {{trigger_accession}} are present in values.json for all three evaluation cases), and otherwise describes the magnitude qualitatively or omits it.
diff_summary: Procedure step 3 only: replaced 'Spell out ordinal words.' with (a) ordinal words allowed only in period names, and (b) a rule forbidding quantities, dates or percentages written in words, with examples taken from the evidence, and the instruction to use a {{key}} when one exists or else describe qualitatively or leave out. No other step, role, acceptance check, gate, limit or policy changes.
expected_effect: Candidate notes have an empty spelled_quantities list, cite the rating bands as {{rating_outperform_min}} / {{rating_underperform_max}} and the cutoff/price date as {{cutoff_utc}} / {{price_date}}, and show no new gate_note blocker (placeholders resolve to code values).
